To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the <;112> orientation tin deposit has the lowest propensity for tin whiskers, the <;321> orientation has the highest propensity for tin whisker, the <;220> has intermediate propensity, the 5-8μm grain tin deposit has the highest propensity and the 1-4 μm grain tin deposit is intermediate.
the <;220> texture is more prone to whisker formation and the <;321> texture is less prone to whisker growth than the <;112> texture.

the <;220> crystal orientation and the 5-8 μ m grain size tin deposits exhibited the lowest whisker propensity in each of the test methods, and that whiskers grew from the <;321> crystal orientation and 1-4 μm grain size tin deposits in all the stress tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of crystal orientation and grain size of matte tin on tin whisker propensity using stress-induced test methods.
the effects of electrodeposited tin crystal orientation and deposit grain structure on whisker growth propensity, and the effects of stress-inducing tests on the whisker growth propensity.
understanding the effect of deposit stress on whisker growth propensity, and the role of crystal orientation and grain size on the stress formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal orientation of the tin deposit has a significant effect on the tin whisker growth rate, while grain size has a minimal effect.
the whisker growth propensity of the <;220> crystal orientation is greater than that of the <;321> crystal orientation.
the whisker growth rate is not a function of the <;112>/<;101> vs. <;220>/<;321> crystal orientation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the whisker growth propensity of tin is affected by the crystal orientation and grain size, and the whiskers grow more readily from the tin with <;220> orientation and 5-8 μ m grain size.

the <;321> crystal orientation and small grain size tin deposits are the most resistant to tin whisker growth, and the <;112> crystal orientation and large grain size tin deposit are the most susceptible.
tin whisker growth is a complex phenomenon, which is dependent upon the combination of the driving forces, deposit stress and deposit properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the whisker growth rate and density is not a function of the specific crystal orientation, but is a function of the grain size.
the crystal orientation of the tin deposit has a greater effect on tin whisker propensity than the grain size of the deposit.
the <;220> orientation tin whisker growth is significantly less than <;321> orientation tin whiskers.
